thread:
alex.k: proposal: add a compatibility proxy + a per-customer 'compat mode' toggle in the console to handle lingering v1 clients. we can route v1 traffic to a lightweight proxy that rewrites headers and enforces a soft qps cap.
  sanjay: curious about billing. if we proxy and reissue requests to v2 models, does customer get charged twice? also worried about double-counting tokens in telemetry.
  alex.k: good call. design is to proxy at the edge and forward with an internal header `X-Compat-Proxy: v1` and a flag that prevents duplicate billing. proxy should strip client-level auth for billing and attribute to the tenant only once. internal meter will mark origin=compat-proxy.
  maria: +1 for console toggle. UX idea: a dashboard tile that shows "Active v1 clients" (sampled), last seen, and a one-click enable for per-tenant compat-mode with a cap slider (e.g., 50 rps). That way product can opt-in while they migrate.
  julie_p: we should also show a migration guidance modal: list top endpoints and example curl to switch to v2. product wants clear CTA before flipping compat-mode.
  alex.k: sample instrumentation plan:
  ```
  // header added by compat proxy
  X-Redwood-Compat: v1-proxy
  X-Redwood-Compat-Client: <client-id>
  ```
  telemetry events: compat.proxy.request (sampled 1%), compat.proxy.migrate_click, compat.proxy.cap_throttled

  sanjay: sampling 1% is fine for volume, but we need deterministic counts for billing and quota enforcement. telemetry should separate sampling for analytics vs. counters for quota/billing which must be exact.

  alex.k: agreed. counters = exact; analytics events = sampled. we'll emit counters for total forwarded tokens and increment tenant quota once. analytics pipeline will also include sampled request payload hashes for debug (PII scrubbed).

  ops-bot: deploy plan created: canary 10% on eu-west, flag=compat-proxy-v1-canal. Ticket: INF-3247

  julie_p: product question: if tenant flips compat-mode off, do we fail requests or route them directly to v2? what's graceful behavior?

  alex.k: behaviour options: (A) direct-break: return 426 upgrade required; (B) auto-upgrade: rewrite request to v2 best-effort; (C) soft-fail: continue proxying for 1h after toggle off. leaning B with telemetry guardrails and a rollout window.

  maria: console UI should default to show expected latency delta and cost estimate for enabling compat-mode vs requiring migration. customers care about cost/latency tradeoffs.

  sanjay: also add an internal alert if compat-proxy queue depth > 50ms P95 increase — we don't want it to become a bottleneck.

  alex.k: noted. instrument metrics: compat.proxy.latency.p50/p95, compat.proxy.queue_depth, compat.proxy.rewrites_per_min, compat.proxy.throttled_per_min. wire to existing routing dashboards and add a tile under 'APIs -> Versioning'.

  julie_p: for rollout: prototype behind feature flag, test canary on two tenants, collect migration acceptance rate over 2 weeks, then enable self-serve in console.

  deploy-bot: canary deploy started by alex.k for compat-proxy-v1-canal at 2834567950. Logs: https://internal.redwood/deploy/INF-3247

  sanjay: one more: schema differences. if v1 schemas map poorly to v2, proxy should be a last-resort shim not a long-term compatibility layer. we should add a TTL to any shimmed tenant (e.g., 90 days) and surface expiration in console.

  alex.k: agreed. TTL show + email nudge three weeks prior to expiry. add console banner and API header `X-Compat-Expires: 2026-06-01` for debug.

  maria: i'll mock the dashboard tile and the migration modal this afternoon and share frames.

  julie_p: thanks. action items: alex protos proxy + metrics, sanjay verifies billing/quotas path, maria design mocks, ops validates canary criteria. sync Friday 11am to review canary telemetry.

  ops-bot: INF-3247 updated: alex.k assigned, due 2026-04-08.
